NASA Advances Nuclear-Powered 'SR-1 Freedom' Spacecraft Ahead of 2028 Launch

28 Oct 2026, 12:03 AM IST · GlobeWire Daily Tech Desk · Source: www.nasa.gov

Key takeaways Progress on Key Propulsion Technology NASA has reached a critical milestone in the development of the SR-1 Freedom, the agency's first fission-powered spacecraft designed for travel beyond Earth's orbit. Recent contract actions have been finalized to accelerate the de

Progress on Key Propulsion Technology

NASA has reached a critical milestone in the development of the SR-1 Freedom, the agency's first fission-powered spacecraft designed for travel beyond Earth's orbit. Recent contract actions have been finalized to accelerate the development of the nuclear power module, a core component of the craft's nuclear electric propulsion system. Sierra Lobo Inc. has been tasked with providing the closed Brayton cycle power conversion system, which will transform thermal energy from the onboard fission reactor into electricity.

Collaborative Engineering for Deep Space

The nuclear power module is a joint effort between NASA and the Department of Energy (DOE). While the conversion system is being developed under NASA’s Space Flight Systems Development and Operations Contract III at the Glenn Research Center, the fission reactor itself is being designed by the DOE’s Idaho National Laboratory. This modular approach aims to demonstrate technology that could eventually support long-term lunar operations, such as powering a Moon Base during periods where solar energy is insufficient.

Safety Protocols and Mission Objectives

Safety remains a central focus for the SR-1 Freedom mission. NASA officials have confirmed that the onboard fission reactor will remain completely inactive throughout the launch phase and will only be activated once the spacecraft has successfully cleared Earth's orbit. The mission is subject to continuous oversight by a NASA chief safety officer and adheres to interagency regulatory standards regarding hazard mitigation and failure tolerance.

Impact and Future Exploration

Scheduled for launch in late 2028, the SR-1 Freedom mission will deploy the 'SkyFall' science package. This consists of three advanced Mars helicopters, which are evolved designs based on the successful Ingenuity platform. These units are intended to conduct scientific reconnaissance, identify potential water sources, and evaluate exploration zones. Readers can track ongoing mission updates and review technical specifications through the official NASA project portal at https://www.nasa.gov/mission/space-reactor-1-freedom/
